verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：我休你们的母亲，休书在哪里呢？我将你们卖给我哪一个债主呢？你们被卖，是因你们的罪孽；你们的母亲被休，是因你们的过犯。
verses.en: This is what the Lord says:“Where is your mother’s divorce certificateby which I divorced her?Or to which of my creditors did I sell you?[NOTE:1] Look, you were sold because of your sins;[NOTE:2] because of your rebellious acts I divorced your mother.[NOTE:3]
notes: The Lord challenges the exiles (Zion’s children) to bring incriminating evidence against him. The rhetorical questions imply that Israel accused the Lord of divorcing his wife (Zion) and selling his children (the Israelites) into slavery to pay off a debt.

The Lord admits that he did sell the Israelites, but it was because of their sins, not because of some debt he owed. If he had sold them to a creditor, they ought to be able to point him out, but the preceding rhetorical question implies they would not be able to do so.

The Lord admits he did divorce Zion, but that too was the result of the nation’s sins. The force of the earlier rhetorical question comes into clearer focus now. The question does not imply that a certificate does not exist and that no divorce occurred. Rather, the question asks for the certificate to be produced so the accuser can see the reason for the divorce in black and white. The Lord did not put Zion away arbitrarily.
verses.commentary:
50:1 There are two ancient legal situations used to highlight Israel's legal standing.

- divorce of a faithless wife (cf. Isa. 54:6-7; Jer. 3:1,8; Hosea 2:4; see SPECIAL TOPIC: CERTIFICATE OF DIVORCE)

- the selling of someone into slavery for a debt (cf. Deut. 32:30; 2 Kgs. 4:1; Neh. 5:5)

For Israel's "iniquities" and "transgressions" she was judged and exiled. It was not the
weakness of YHWH, but the rebellion of His people (cf. Isa. 59:2).

▣ "you were sold for your iniquities" This is the exact opposite of the imagery of ransom/redeem.

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

verses.zh: 我来的时候，为何无人等候呢？我呼唤的时候，为何无人答应呢？我的膀臂岂是缩短、不能救赎吗？我岂无拯救之力吗？看哪，我一斥责，海就干了；我使江河变为旷野；其中的鱼因无水腥臭，干渴而死。
verses.en: Why does no one challenge me when I come?Why does no one respond when I call?[NOTE:1] Is my hand too weak[NOTE:2] to deliver[NOTE:3] you?Do I lack the power to rescue you?Look, with a mere shout[NOTE:4] I can dry up the sea;I can turn streams into a desert,so the fish rot away and die from lack of water.[NOTE:5]
notes: The present-tense translation of the verbs assumes that the Lord is questioning why Israel does not attempt to counter his arguments. Another possibility is to take the verbs as referring to past events: “Why did no one meet me when I came? Why did no one answer when I called?” In this case the Lord might be asking why Israel rejected his calls to repent and his offer to deliver them.
Heb “short” (so NAB, NASB, NIV).
Or “ransom” (NAB, NASB, NIV84); NIV11 “deliver.”
Heb “with my rebuke.”
Heb “the fish stink from lack of water and die from thirst.”
verses.commentary:
50:2 This verse starts with a series of four rhetorical questions, as Isa. 50:1 had two. The
first two deal with YHWH, surprised at the lack of intercession and faith response.

He asks if Israel had lost confidence in His ability to save!

▣ "Is My hand so short" This is a Qal PERFECT and a Qal
INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the same root (BDB 894, KB 1126), which intensifies a concept,
here a question.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN

▣ "ransom" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM. It is parallel to "deliver."

▣ "sea. . .rivers" See SPECIAL TOPIC: WATERS/SEA.

verses.zh: 我使诸天以黑暗为衣服，以麻布为遮盖。
verses.en: I can clothe the sky in darkness;I can cover it with sackcloth.”
verses.commentary:
50:3 "I clothe the heavens with blackness" This probably relates to YHWH creating the heavenly
lights in Genesis 1. Often in the Bible, when He visits His creation for blessing or judgment, these heavenly
lights are affected (cf. Job 9:5-9; Isa. 13:10; 24:23; 50:3; Ezek. 32:7; Joel 2:2,10,31; 3:15; Matt. 13:24-25;
24:29; Luke 21:25; Rev. 6:12-13).

▣ "make sackcloth their covering" See SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES.

verses.zh: 主耶和华赐我受教者的舌头，使我知道怎样用言语扶助疲乏的人。主每早晨提醒，提醒我的耳朵，使我能听，像受教者一样。
verses.en: The Sovereign Lord has given me the capacity to be his spokesman,[NOTE:1] so that I know how to help the weary.[NOTE:2] He wakes me up every morning;he makes me alert so I can listen attentively as disciples do.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “has given to me a tongue of disciples.”sn Verses 4-11 contain the third of the so-called servant songs, which depict the career of the Lord’s special servant, envisioned as an ideal Israel (49:3) who rescues the exiles and fulfills God’s purposes for the world. Here the servant alludes to opposition (something hinted at in 49:4), but also expresses his determination to persevere with the Lord’s help.

Heb “to know [?] the weary with a word.” Comparing it with Arabic and Aramaic cognates yields the meaning of “help, sustain.” Nevertheless, the meaning of עוּת (ʿut) is uncertain. The word occurs only here in the OT (see BDB 736 s.v.). Various scholars have suggested an emendation to עָנוֹת (ʿanot) from עָנָה (ʿanah, “answer”): “so that I know how to respond kindly to the weary.” Since the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa and the Vulgate support the MT reading, that reading is retained.
Heb “he arouses for me an ear, to hear like disciples.”
verses.commentary:
50:4-6 These verses describe aspects of the Servant's ministry (in His own words).

- gifted to listen

- gifted to encourage, Isa. 50:4a

- He listens to

- hurting, weary ones (cf. Jer. 31:25), Isa. 50:4b

- YHWH, Isa. 50:4c,d,5a

- He was not disobedient, Isa. 50:5b

- He did not turn back, Isa. 50:5c

- He yielded Himself to abuse by leaders (cf. Matt. 26:67; 27:30; Mark 15:19)

- whipped His back

- plucked out His beard

- spit in His face

The Servant's verbal skills will lead to a rejection of His message and person
by those who refuse to listen (cf. Isa. 50:11).

50:4a "The Lord God" This is literally two words.

- Adon ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord (adon and kurios)

- YHWH ‒ see SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.

The reason to translate them in this way is because they are both often translated, "Lord."
Lord Lord would be confusing to English speakers (e.g. Ps. 110:1, "The
Lord says to my Lord," which is quoted in Matt. 22:44; Mark 12:36; Luke 20:42;
Acts 2:34,35; Heb. 1:13).

▣ "disciples" This is a rare word (BDB 541), found only here (twice) and Isa. 8:16 in
this sense. Usually it is translated "taught" (Isa. 54:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: DISCIPLES

50:4b

NASB, NRSV
"sustain the weary one"

NKJV
"speak a word in season to him who is weary"

TEV
"strengthen the weary"

NJB
"to give a word of comfort to the weary"

JPSOA
"speak timely words to the weary"

REB
"to console the weary"

The MT (reflected in the NASB) has a rare Hebrew VERBAL
(BDB 736, KB 804, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT), which occurs only here in this
form. BDB suggests the text is corrupt and may have originally read "edify."

- לעות ‒ BDB 736, "help"

- לרעות ‒ BDB, KB, "edify"

But, the DSS and the Vulgate support the MT. The NET Bible mentions that cognate roots
in Arabic and Aramaic mean "help" or "sustain."

Remember, in these cases of rare roots or stems, the context, especially parallelism,
helps to suggest the meanings. The central truth of the strophe is the important issue in interpretation.

50:4c,d There is a repeated Hiphil IMPERFECT (BDB 734, KB 802), "awakens."
In the Hiphil it is used to rouse or stir up activity.

- Isa. 13:17 ‒ the Medes (Jer. 51:11)

- Isa. 41:2,25 ‒ Cyrus II

- Isa. 45:13 ‒ Cyrus II

- here ‒ the Servant

- Dan. 11:2 ‒ inter-biblical ruler

YHWH is in control of world history and world redemption!

50:5a This is literally "has opened my ear," which seems to refer to

- a clear message received

- an allusion to obedience, to which the next two parallel poetic lines attest

This would surely describe Jesus' obedience to the Father's will (i.e. Matt. 26:39; John 8:29; 14:31;
15:10; Phil. 2:8; Heb. 5:8; 10:7 [quotes Ps. 40:8]).

verses.zh: 主耶和华开通我的耳朵；我并没有违背，也没有退后。
verses.en: The Sovereign Lord has spoken to me clearly;[NOTE:1] I have not rebelled,I have not turned back.
notes: Or perhaps, “makes me obedient.” The text reads literally, “has opened for me an ear.”

verses.zh: 人打我的背，我任他打；人拔我腮颊的胡须，我由他拔；人辱我，吐我，我并不掩面。
verses.en: I offered my back to those who attacked,[NOTE:1] my jaws to those who tore out my beard;I did not hide my facefrom insults and spitting.
notes: Or perhaps, “who beat [me].”
verses.commentary:
50:6 The specific treatment of the obedient Servant is a foreshadowing of the treatment
of Jesus. This introduces the fourth Servant Song in Isa. 52:13-53:12, esp. Isa. 50:3,4-5,7-9. The Servant
will pay a high price for His loyalty, trust, and obedience to YHWH (cf. Psalm 2; 22). There is a divine purpose
in suffering for Him (cf. Isaiah 53; Mark 10:45; 2 Cor. 5:21; the book of Hebrews).

SPECIAL TOPIC: A SUFFERING MESSIAH

verses.zh: 主耶和华必帮助我，所以我不抱愧。我硬着脸面好像坚石；我也知道我必不致蒙羞。
verses.en: But the Sovereign Lord helps me,so I am not humiliated.For that reason I am steadfastly resolved;[NOTE:1] I know I will not be put to shame.
notes: Heb “Therefore I set my face like flint.”
verses.commentary:
50:7-9 The first verse of this strophe is repeated in Isa. 50:9a, "the Lord (Adon)
God (YHWH) helps me."

Because of this the Servant will

- not be disgraced

- set His face like flint (cf. Luke 9:51)

- be ashamed

Why, because YHWH acts on His behalf, introduced by another series of questions
(Isa. 50:8-9). The grammatical structure (i.e. "Who. . .?") runs through Isa. 50:10.

verses.zh: 称我为义的与我相近；谁与我争论，可以与我一同站立；谁与我作对，可以就近我来。
verses.en: The one who vindicates me is close by.Who dares to argue with me? Let us confront each other![NOTE:1] Who is my accuser?[NOTE:2] Let him challenge me![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “Let us stand together!”
Heb “Who is the master of my judgment?”
Heb “let him approach me”; NAB, NIV “Let him confront me.”
verses.commentary:
50:8

NASB, NRSV
"vindicates"

NKJV, LXX, Peshitta
"justifies"

TEV
"prove me innocent"

NJB
"saving justice"

JPSOA
"My vindicator"

REB
"will clear my name"

As Isa. 50:6-7 describe an unjust trial, so Isa. 50:8 describes a just verdict. The
VERB (BDB 842, KB 1003) is a Hiphil PARTICIPLE which means
"declare righteous" (cf. Exod. 23:7; Deut. 25:1; 1 Kgs. 8:32; Prov. 17:15). It is used in a negative context
in Isa. 5:23. It describes

- God in this context

- the Servant in Isa. 53:11

▣ "Let him draw near to Me" This is a Qal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense. The VERB (BDB 620, KB 670) is used of approaching a
judge at trial. Notice here the Servant is the Judge (i.e. "Let him draw near to Me").

The imagery of a court scene is one of three prophetic models. Often YHWH is depicted
in various roles.

- as the Judge ‒ 1 Sam. 24:15; Ps. 9:4; 43:1; 140:12; Lam. 3:58; Micah 7:9

- as the accused ‒ Isa. 50:1-3; 49:14

- as advocate of the weak ‒ Prov. 23:11

- as advocate of Israel ‒ Ps. 119:54; Isa. 50:8-9; 51:22; Jer. 50:34; 51:36

- as litigant ‒ Ps. 74:22; Isa. 41:21; 43:5; Jer. 25:9

- against Israel ‒ Ps. 103:9; Isa. 3:13-15; Jer. 2:9; Hosea 4:1-4; 12:2; Micah 6:1-5

50:9a.b These first two lines of poetry express a repeated truth (cf. Ps. 118:6; Rom. 8:31-39; Heb. 13:6).

verses.zh: 主耶和华要帮助我；谁能定我有罪呢？他们都像衣服渐渐旧了，为蛀虫所咬。
verses.en: Look, the Sovereign Lord helps me.Who dares to condemn me?Look, all of them will wear out like clothes;a moth will eat away at them.

verses.zh: 你们中间谁是敬畏耶和华、听从他仆人之话的？这人行在暗中，没有亮光。当倚靠耶和华的名，仗赖自己的　神。
verses.en: Who among you fears the Lord?Who obeys[NOTE:1] his servant?Whoever walks in deep darkness,[NOTE:2] without light,should trust in the name of the Lordand rely on his God.
notes: Heb “[who] listens to the voice of his servant?” The interrogative is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
The plural indicates degree. Darkness may refer to exile and/or moral evil.
verses.commentary:
50:10-11 AB takes these two verses as a response to the Servant (p. 116), apparently
by YHWH (Leupold, p. 196). There is a contrast between two kinds of "light."

- the darkness (PLURAL for intensity) of those who have faith in God and
His Messiah but do not fully understand (Isa. 50:10)

- let him trust in the name of the Lord ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (BDB 105, KB 120)
used in a JUSSIVE sense (see SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH)

- let him rely on his God ‒ Niphal IMPERFECT (BDB 1043, KB 1612) used in a
JUSSIVE sense

- those who make their own light (i.e. fire, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE) and
walk in it (Qal IMPERATIVE) which will eventually consume them (i.e. lie down
in torment, Isa. 50:11)

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHERE ARE THE DEAD?

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

verses.zh: 凡你们点火，用火把围绕自己的可以行在你们的火焰里，并你们所点的火把中。这是我手所定的：你们必躺在悲惨之中。
verses.en: Look, all of you who start a fireand who equip yourselves with[NOTE:1] flaming arrows,[NOTE:2] walk[NOTE:3] in the light[NOTE:4] of the fire you startedand among the flaming arrows you ignited![NOTE:5] This is what you will receive from me:[NOTE:6] You will lie down in a place of pain.[NOTE:7]
notes: Several more recent commentators have proposed an emendation of מְאַזְּרֵי (meʾazzere, “who put on”) to מְאִירִי (meʾiri, “who light”). However, both Qumran scrolls of Isaiah and the Vulgate support the MT reading (cf. NIV, ESV).
On the meaning of זִיקוֹת (ziqot, “flaming arrows”), see HALOT 268 s.v. זִיקוֹת.
The imperative is probably rhetorical and has a predictive force.
Or perhaps, “flame” (so ASV).
Perhaps the servant here speaks to his enemies and warns them that they will self-destruct.
Heb “from my hand” (so NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).

The imagery may be that of a person who becomes ill and is forced to lie down in pain on a sickbed. Some see this as an allusion to a fiery place of damnation because of the imagery employed earlier in the verse.

"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This chapter contains the third Servant Song (Isa. 50:4-11).

- In Isa. 49:25d the court imagery is used with the Servant as the defense advocate. Here the
court imagery is used of YHWH as divorcing His covenant people for their faithlessness.

- In contrast to the faithlessness of the covenant people, the faithfulness of the Servant, the
ideal Israelite, is stressed. He will accomplish what Israel could not!

- Notice that most English translations see three paragraphs in Isa. 50:4-11, which would
denote three main truths.

- Isa. 50:4-6

- Isa. 50:7-9

- Isa. 50:10-11
